findings.evidence: New CHECK macro formats the message with `char _detail[512]; std::snprintf(_detail, sizeof(_detail), __VA_ARGS__);`, while many call sites pass whole log dumps as the message, e.g. `CHECK(logHas(...), "banner crc32 / missing-ini defaults ...:\n%s", readLog().c_str());` (line 180) and the same pattern at lines 200, 219, 401, 466. The old macro wrote these with fprintf and no size limit.
findings.suggested_investigation: Run gate_test with a deliberately failing check whose readLog() output exceeds 512 bytes (e.g. add a temporary CHECK(false, "%s", readLog().c_str()) after a few HOLD/INSTANT lines) and confirm the printed detail is truncated. If so, consider sizing the detail buffer to the message or streaming it to stderr, but do not change the harness without a fresh gate PASS.
findings.why_it_matters: On a failing check, any log dump longer than ~511 bytes is cut off silently (snprintf truncates without error). The failure is still counted, so the exit code is not affected, but the diagnostic output that the log-dump messages exist to show is lost exactly when it is needed.

findings.evidence: `#define CHECK(c, ...) do { ... char _what[128]; std::snprintf(_what, sizeof(_what), "%s:%d: %s", tag, key, #c); ::kt::Check(_what, ...` — the stringified condition is embedded in a 128-byte buffer alongside tag (up to 47 chars) and key. The long condition at line 131, `before.ok && before.featsOk && before.spellsOk && before.deltasOk && samePend(before.pd, in)`, is about 90 characters, so tag + key + condition exceeds 128 bytes.
findings.suggested_investigation: Force a failure at line 131 (for example by corrupting the fake pending record) and check whether the printed check name is cut before the condition's end. If truncation is confirmed, the buffer size in the CHECK macro is the place to look; the kt::Check implementation (TestHarness.h, not in this packet's directory and not verified here) should be checked for how it prints the name.
findings.why_it_matters: The check name reported on failure is truncated, which can make it harder to tell which of several similar assertions failed (line 131 and 136 share prefixes). The pass/fail result itself is unaffected, so this is a diagnostic-quality risk, not a gate weakening.
